skill.name: defi-expert
skill.description: Guides DeFi protocol integration work by checking token decimals, amount denominations, address formats, and protocol-specific data conventions.
skill.summary: Review DeFi integration details before writing or debugging protocol code.
skill.author: BarisSozen

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive from a TypeScript Markdown code fence in SKILL.md. The skill is prompt-only and provides DeFi integration guidance without executable code or prompt injection content.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 59 starts a TypeScript Markdown code block that shows DeFi amount handling examples. It is documentation text, not Ruby shell backtick execution or an executable command path.

content.value_statement: DeFi integrations often fail because token units, decimals, and protocol formats are easy to mix up. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through checks for safer protocol code.
actual_capabilities: Checks token decimal assumptions for assets such as USDC, USDT, WBTC, ETH, and DAI.
Explains denomination choices such as wei, ray, wad, and basis points.
Reviews DeFi code for common amount parsing and precision mistakes.
Prompts validation of checksummed addresses before protocol integration work.
Focuses on Aave, Compound, Uniswap, Curve, Balancer, swaps, liquidations, and flash loans.
limitations: Does not fetch live token metadata or protocol documentation by itself.
Does not replace formal smart contract security review.
Does not execute transactions, deploy contracts, or verify on-chain state.
Requires users to provide the relevant protocol, asset, and code context.

use_cases.title: Prepare a protocol integration
use_cases.description: Check required units, token decimals, and address handling before implementing a DeFi adapter.

use_cases.title: Review amount handling bugs
use_cases.description: Find likely precision errors when balances, health factors, rates, or swap amounts look incorrect.

use_cases.title: Validate integration requirements
use_cases.description: Build a checklist of data formats and protocol assumptions before assigning implementation work.

prompt_templates.title: Check Token Units
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this DeFi task for token decimal and denomination risks. Protocol: [protocol]. Assets: [assets]. Planned operation: [operation].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review before writing integration code

prompt_templates.title: Review Amount Parsing
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this amount handling logic for DeFi precision mistakes. Explain any decimal, wei, ray, wad, or basis point issues in plain language.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate code review for token amount conversions

prompt_templates.title: Debug Protocol Values
prompt_templates.prompt: Help debug this DeFi value mismatch. Expected result: [expected]. Actual result: [actual]. Protocol fields and raw values: [details].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate troubleshooting for rates, balances, or health factors

prompt_templates.title: Design Integration Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a DeFi integration checklist for [protocol] and [operation]. Include token decimals, denominations, address validation, API structures, and failure cases.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a production integration

output_examples.input: Review a USDC swap integration that uses 18 decimals for every token.
output_examples.output: The review flags USDC as a 6-decimal token and recommends asset-specific parsing. It also asks for checksummed addresses and slippage basis point validation.

output_examples.input: Debug an Aave health factor display that divides the raw value by one quintillion.
output_examples.output: The response explains that Aave rates commonly use ray precision. It recommends using the correct 27-decimal scaling before displaying the health factor.

output_examples.input: Prepare a checklist for adding a Balancer pool integration.
output: Confirm token decimals for every pool asset.
Verify amount units expected by each contract call.
Validate addresses and pool identifiers before implementation.

best_practices: Provide the target protocol, assets, and operation before asking for review.
Include raw values and expected display values when debugging precision issues.
Verify token decimals from trusted sources before final implementation.
anti_patterns: Do not assume every ERC-20 token uses 18 decimals.
Do not mix wei, ray, wad, and basis points without explicit conversion.
Do not treat this skill as a substitute for a full security audit.

faq.question: What protocols does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Aave, Compound, Uniswap, Curve, Balancer, and common DeFi operations such as swaps, liquidations, and flash loans.

faq.question: Can it verify live token decimals?
faq.answer: No. It reminds users to verify decimals and can reason from provided data, but it does not fetch live metadata by itself.

faq.question: Does it write smart contracts?
faq.answer: It can guide protocol integration code, but it mainly reviews formats, units, and assumptions around DeFi logic.

faq.question: Can it replace a DeFi security audit?
faq.answer: No. It helps catch common integration mistakes, but formal audit work requires broader testing and expert review.

faq.question: Why does it mention Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The skill is designed for AI coding assistants that help developers plan, review, and debug DeFi integration work.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the protocol, assets, token decimals if known, raw values, expected outputs, and the relevant code or integration plan.
